definitions.gloss: wasted effort; fruitless labor; vain attempt
definitions.explanation: Effort or trouble that produces no result. Emphasizes the futility of the work expended.

examples.japanese: {結局|けっきょく}、{無駄骨|むだぼね}に{終|お}わった。
examples.english: In the end, it turned out to be a wasted effort.

examples.japanese: わざわざ{行|い}ったのに{無駄骨|むだぼね}だった。
examples.english: I went out of my way to go, but it was all for nothing.

examples.japanese: {無駄骨|むだぼね}を{折|お}らないように、{事前|じぜん}に{確認|かくにん}しておいたほうがいい。
examples.english: You should check in advance so you don't waste your efforts.

notes:
Compound of {無駄|むだ} (futile, useless) + {骨|ほね} (bone; effort, trouble). The {骨|ほね} here refers to effort or labor (as in {骨|ほね}を{折|お}る, "to make an effort"), so {無駄骨|むだぼね} literally means "useless effort."

USAGE:
Most commonly appears in the expression {無駄骨|むだぼね}を{折|お}る (to waste one's efforts) or {無駄骨|むだぼね}に{終|お}わる (to end up being a wasted effort). Often used when someone went to considerable trouble only to achieve nothing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無駄骨|むだぼね}を{折|お}る — to waste one's efforts
- {無駄骨|むだぼね}に{終|お}わる — to end in wasted effort
- {無駄骨|むだぼね}だった — it was a wasted effort

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {徒労|とろう} — futile effort (more literary/formal)
- {骨折|ほねお}り{損|ぞん} — effort that went unrewarded (emphasizes the loss)
- {無駄足|むだあし} — wasted trip (specifically about going somewhere for nothing)
